text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were slightly down in late dealings marked by an uneven market. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.32, down 0.37 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts drifted lower on Monday following Bunds with little of domestic interest to impact the market until UK monetary meeting on Wednesday. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-22/32, down 15/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures took their direction from the Bund market on Monday and drifted gently lower throughout the session amid subdued volume and caution ahead of week packed with U.S. data releases. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.30 down 0.18 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures sharply pared earlier gains and closed near support just off day's lows after turning into negative territory in afternoon business on a wave of profit-taking after failing to test highs, traders said. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.21 down 0.87 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries were slightly lower in late morning trade. The Fed added reserves via 4-day fixed system repurchases. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-27/32, down 05/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.83 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures contract made new headway in uncharted territory after setting a new all-time high for any benchmark futures contract by Monday's Tokyo close. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 124.54, down 0.15 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market wasted little time on Monday, with a host of deals emerging in the morning session headed by Brazil's expected debut global bond. Brazil launched its $750 million five-year issue at a 265 basis points yield spread over U.S. Treasuries. J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg will finalise prcing later today.
